# The Restaurant AP Automation Benchmark Report: Summer 2026 Edition


**by Mike Waldron**


## Why This Report Exists


Restaurants operate on the combined impact of prime, food, and labor costs, which don’t leave much room for waste. When prime costs creep above 65 to 70 percent of revenue, margin pressure shows up fast. A broadliner invoice with a mispriced case of chicken, or a vendor quietly creeping prices across hundreds of SKUs, isn’t a paperwork problem. It’s the gap between theoretical and actual food cost, and that gap is where operators look for waste, theft, or billing errors.


Most operators sense when something’s off. Food cost percentage looks high this month, but proving whether that’s a recipe issue, a vendor billing error, or a coding mistake takes a level-by-level review most AP teams don’t have time for. That gap between sensing a problem and proving it is where restaurant AP has always struggled.


We process tens of thousands of invoices every quarter across our restaurant customer base. This report is what that data actually shows, not industry estimates, not survey responses, but numbers pulled from real restaurant operations.


This is the first edition. Twice a year, we’ll track how these numbers move, flag what’s driving the changes, and give restaurant operators a benchmark they can actually use. This edition covers duplicate detection, fraud exposure, invoice discrepancies, payment errors, invoice lifecycle time, and AP labor savings.


## Profitability Benchmarks


### Duplicate Detection


**Benchmark** : Restaurant customers were saved $817 million on 1.11 million duplicate invoices flagged and prevented.


In the first half of 2026, restaurant accounts caught 349,000 duplicates, preventing $321 million in overspending.


Restaurants remain the highest-volume duplicate detection segment across our entire customer base. That alone makes the case: at this volume, manually catching duplicate invoices isn’t a realistic line of defense. Automated detection is doing work no AP team could do by hand.


### Invoice Risk


**Benchmark** : 34.8 percent of restaurant clients had at least one invoice flagged for overcharges or fraud, totaling $91.5 million in exposure.


In the first half of 2026, 51 percent of restaurant accounts had a flagged invoice.


The percentage of accounts with flagged invoices increased dramatically. With this large increase, it is clear that the overall pace of risk is still outrunning what manual review alone could ever catch. It is more important than ever to have a system that will automatically flag phishy invoices for review.


### Credit Recovery


**Benchmark:** Ottimate uncovered $420.7 million in credits related to refunds, adjustments, and overcharge corrections last year.


In the first half of 2026, Ottimate uncovered $256.7 million in credits related to refunds, adjustments, and overcharges for restaurants alone.


With continuous price increases and rising invoice volumes, we continue to see overcharges increase. Implementing automation in your workflow is more important than ever to ensure you catch these costly mistakes before they hit your bottom line.


### Payments


**Benchmark** : Ottimate caught 14,250 payments with errors last year, accounting for $1.6 million in potential losses.


So far this year, Ottimate has caught 6,026 payments with errors, accounting for $1.01 million in potential losses.


Payment errors are costly and difficult to recover from once funds have left the account. Halfway through the year, restaurant accounts are already closing in on last year’s full total. Manual payment reviews miss what automated checks catch consistently, which is exactly why a final validation layer before disbursement matters.


## Productivity Benchmarks


### Invoice Lifecycle Time


**Benchmark** : Restaurant customers using Ottimate have reduced invoice lifecycle time from upload to approval from 11 days down to 5.1 days on average.


In the first half of 2026, that number dropped to 2.2days.


Invoice lifecycle time continues to improve quarter after quarter, even as volume increases. That combination, faster processing alongside rising invoice counts, points to platform maturity across this segment, not just early-stage gains that level off.


### AP Labor Savings


**Benchmark** : Ottimate saves restaurant groups $35,200 per account per year in labor costs by reducing the invoice lifecycle.


In the first half of 2026, restaurant customers saved 8.8 days per invoice, up from 5.9 days a year ago, while processing 16 percent more invoices per account.


Faster processing and rising volume are compounding each other. The original labor-savings benchmark now looks conservative relative to what current accounts are actually realizing.


## About This Report


The Restaurant AP Automation Benchmark Report: Summer 2026 Edition is published by Ottimate using aggregated, anonymized data from our restaurant customer base. All benchmarks reflect real invoice processing data across independent restaurants and multi-unit restaurant groups. This is the first edition; future editions will track trends and flag what’s driving the changes.
